# Quarterly operations report — May–July 2026

## Summary

The quarter closed at €1,233,225 in revenue against €467,640 in costs, for a
net result of €765,585 and a 62.1% margin. Revenue grew 4.6% in June before
falling back 9.6% in July, leaving the quarter dependent on a strong start:
May and June together carried the result, while July came in below every
other month. Costs were essentially flat from June onward (€158,240 vs
€158,280), so the July revenue decline flowed almost entirely to the bottom
line. Customer acquisition weakened through the quarter — new signings fell
from 86 in May to 63 in July while churn rose from 17 to 31 — though the
quarter still added 153 net new customers. Support held up well throughout,
closing 95.6% of the 1,001 tickets opened.

## Key figures

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Quarterly revenue | €1,233,225 |
| Quarterly costs | €467,640 |
| Net | €765,585 |
| Margin | 62.1% |
| Net customer adds | 153 |
| Ticket close rate | 95.5% |
| June revenue growth | 4.6% |
| July revenue growth | −9.6% |

## Notes

Two items worth leadership attention. First, the June report is internally
inconsistent: its cost line items sum to €158,540, €300 above the stated
total of €158,240. This report uses the stated totals; the discrepancy is
small enough that the margin is unaffected at one decimal place (62.1% either
way), but finance should confirm which figure is correct. Second, the
combination of falling signings and rising churn across all three months,
alongside the 9.6% July revenue decline, suggests the July dip is a trend
rather than a one-off — cloud costs also climbed each month (€21,310 →
€23,940 → €24,760), compressing an otherwise healthy margin.
